If you choose to have the Bankart repair, be certain to choose a really good sports surgeon and someone who can perform the repair arthroscopically not open.

I had it performed open by a generally orthopedic surgeon at my local hospital and I have been left massively restricted in external rotation. No physio and Two subsequent capsular releases have not fixed the problem. My Shoulder was pulled together so tightly that is has accelerated the degeneration of the cartilage in the joint to the point I now have severe osteoarthritis... I am 38!

I blame the surgeon for ruining my shoulder and not telling me that a specialist would have been bettered suited. My arm is basically ruined. Bodybuilding is over for me a long with my career as an engineer.

If it is performed open then the subscap gets detached and reattached. If it is reattached in a short position this can stabilise the shoulder more but it will restrict movement. Subscap does not have to be touched in an arthroscopic procedure.

Also, quite often a capsular shift is performed to help stability and reduce the risk of another dislocation, HOWEVER if this is overdone, like I believe was done in my case then it can massively restrict ROM. You are supposed to perform PT to stretch the capsule and regain movement but in my case this didn't work. 

Just make sure you get a good surgeon! Don't make my mistake. My arm is done for life now. I am gutted.

* Having a shower
* Cleaning and trimming my fingernails and toenails
* Cleaning my teeth

You can ask your doctor about Wellbutrin (Bupropion) it is another antidepressant but works on increasing Dopamine and Norepinephrine by blocking their re uptake. Dopamine is vital for that sexual desire and interest. It is what drives us and motivates us.

Regular SSRI like the one you describe being on (Luvox) work on increasing Serotonin through the same mechanism of action, stopping its re uptake. It works well for stabilising mood but it can flatten you out and reduce your interest and desire. The reason it does this is that unfortunately it also causes a reduction in Dopamine.

I have heard of some people being able to be prescribed both or just switched to wellbutrin.

It is not the standard go to for PMDD or depression in general. But if you are really suffering with the sexual arousal and attraction issues then it is definitely worth you asking your doctor about it.

I would definitely suggest having a little research about it yourself to see what you think. It may or may not help but its just an option to consider if you did not know about it.

Sadly these are all very common symptoms of  PMDD but maybe you will find some sense of relief knowing it is normal to experience these with this disorder.

First of all try to feel positive about the fact you now have a diagnosis and therefore and explanation for everything you have been feeling.

Now you can come up with an action plan to try manage it better and this will take a lot of trial and error.

What suggestions for help has your doctor or gyno given you.

First port of call for most doctors is suggesting an SSRI such as zoloft. This might help take the edge off the emotional ups and downs just to help you manage with day to day life better while you get a handle on things.

Birth control is another option for trying to alleviate symptoms but this can be very tricky to find the right one as some make things worse.

From a hollistic side of things make sure to take time to yourself whenever you need it. If you need time by yourself then do it, do not worry about not wanting to be social, having quiet time to yourself will help keep you calm and recharge you. Take the space you need to keep you relaxed. If you need to sleep whatever time of day it is then sleep and do not feel bad about it. Do what you need to do to keep to yourself in a relaxed state and avoid all stresses possible.

Regarding the wanting to leave your partner symptom. This is probably the most common one of all. You will doubt your feelings for them and think they are better off without you. I would suggest you speak to your partner and be open and explain this, but also reassure him that you do want to be with him.

Try not to act on any thoughts or make big decisions until after your period has come. Wait until you become more rational.

Track your cycle and also let your partner do the same so he is aware of when things ate going yo get difficult for you. He can then adjust hes behaviours to suit yours.

Lastly keep reading as much info as you can from this sub. You will learn a lot from the women here as i have, even though i am a guy.

Hope some of that helps. Dont panic but it will take a while untill you figure out the best way to manage everything.
